question.text: Kaveri Macro Fund (Cat III AIF) follows an 'absolute-return' strategy — uncorrelated long-short global macro bets using index derivatives. The PPM pre-specifies a benchmark. As per Chapter 8.8, which of the following is the CORRECT benchmarking approach for such an absolute-return Cat III AIF?

answer.text: Nifty 50 TRI is mandatory because it is the broadest market benchmark in India
A fixed pre-determined rate (e.g., 10 percent per annum) specified by the Investment Manager at fund-launch time, not a relative market-index benchmark
The weighted average of sector indices in which the fund trades
Gross long exposure * Nifty 50 TRI minus Gross short exposure * Nifty 50 TRI

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 8.8: 'The benchmark for absolute-return strategies may be fixed rate, pre-determined by the Investment Manager at the time of launching the fund scheme, such as 10 percent per annum. Absolute Returns are not benchmarked against a broad-based market index or a relative benchmark.' This is the workbook's stated rule for global-macro, market-neutral and similar absolute-return Cat III strategies. The Trap: Option A is wrong — the workbook explicitly says absolute-return funds are NOT benchmarked against a broad market index like Nifty 50 TRI. Option C (sector-weighted) applies to thematic long-only composite benchmarks (like Fund Y in Example 8.7), not absolute-return strategies. Option D is an internal exposure computation, not a PPM-level benchmark. Note: The PPM must pre-specify the absolute-return benchmark at fund launch, per Section 8.8.
